claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake an older execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts (so a queued execution waiting behind a running CodeBuild `pulumi up` stage can be superseded and never run).
In CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode, waiting executions form a queue and each one runs in turn.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (pipeline type V2).
The AWS CLI `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands accept `executionMode` and `pipelineType` settings in the pipeline definition.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider has `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The page links /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ as the aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource documentation, and states it is described below on the page.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from deploying to the same stack.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is set on the stage that references the environment with the exclusive lock check.
The Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` setting accepts `sequential` and `runLatest`, and `runLatest` is the default.
With the Azure Pipelines exclusive lock's `runLatest` behavior, only the most recently queued run acquires the lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over rather than eventually applied.
With the Azure Pipelines exclusive lock's `sequential` behavior, every queued stage run acquires the lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, one at a time in order (analogous to sequential lock behavior).
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The linked page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ and registry page /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exist.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command: up`, `stack`, and `args` (e.g., `--yes`).
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs target the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
The page links to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ as the page describing update conflicts.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" option is 0, meaning unlimited.
With TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" set to 1, a second build that would otherwise start immediately is queued behind the first and runs only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives the same one-at-a-time behavior as limiting TeamCity to one simultaneous build.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes deployments, with `lockBehavior: sequential` set on the stage.
The YAML stage-level property `lockBehavior` in Azure Pipelines accepts the value `sequential`.
The Pulumi Azure DevOps continuous-delivery guide has a section titled 'Serialize deployments with an exclusive lock' (anchor #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock).
AWS CodePipeline supports a pipeline execution mode setting with value `QUEUED`, which makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi AWS Code Services continuous-delivery guide has a section 'Serialize pipeline executions' (anchor #serialize-pipeline-executions).
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on a build configuration serializes deployment builds.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi TeamCity continuous-delivery guide has a section 'Limit concurrent builds' (anchor #limit-concurrent-builds).
